note: Majority: null. The Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 2 of 2016 (Laws.Africa's copy of the gazetted act, read 2026-10-31), art. 266, defines an adult as one who has attained, or is above, nineteen; a child as one who has attained, or is below, eighteen; a young person as one from fifteen to below nineteen; art. 46 gives the vote at eighteen. No statute setting the age of contractual capacity was read (Parliament's site, parliament.gov.zm, and the labour ministry's did not answer; ZambiaLII answered behind Cloudflare), so majority isn't held; 19 (the constitutional adult) is the likely reading and is left for a source. Work: the Employment Code Act No. 3 of 2019 (FAOLEX's copy of the gazetted act), Part V: s. 80 takes 'child' and 'young person' from the Constitution; s. 81 no child in an industrial undertaking; s. 82(1) no child in a covered work site (any public or private, commercial, agricultural or domestic workplace), s. 82(2) save light work by a child between thirteen and fifteen; s. 84 a young person (15 to 18) may work in an industrial undertaking only as an apprentice or with an authorised officer's certificate; s. 86 no night work. The form holds 15, the age a young person may be employed (my reading: the Act's own text, read with the Constitution's overlapping definitions, never states 15 as the general minimum in so many words; the US Department of Labor's 2019 report reads it the same way). Performers: s. 82(3)(a): the ban doesn't apply to a child's participation in artistic performances in accordance with a statutory instrument issued by the Minister prescribing the hours and conditions. The form holds free; whether such an instrument has been made was not read. Service: null. The 2016 amendment's article on a citizen's duties makes it a citizen's duty to provide national, defence and military service when called upon by the State, but no conscription law or defence ministry page was read.

sources.title: Constitution of Zambia (Amendment) Act No. 2 of 2016 (gazetted text, Laws.Africa commons)
sources.said: “ adult ” means a person who has attained, or is above, the age of nineteen years ... “ child ” means a person who has attained, or is below, the age of eighteen years ... “ young person ” means a person who has attained the age of fifteen years, but is below the age of nineteen years

sources.title: Employment Code Act No. 3 of 2019 (gazetted text, FAOLEX)
sources.said: Subject to subsection (2), a person shall not employ a child in a covered work site. (2) Despite subsection (1), a child aged between thirteen and fifteen years may be engaged in light work ... (3) Subsection (1) shall not apply to— (a) work constituting the participation of the child in artistic performances in accordance with a statutory instrument, issued by the Minister
